text: One tiny letter can change a whole word. Listen: cap. Cape.
Cap has a short a sound. When silent e joins the end, the a says its name: cape.
The final e is quiet, but it changes the vowel sound.
Watch the pattern again. Kit has a short i sound.
Add silent e. The i becomes long: kite.
The spelling changed, the sound changed, and the meaning changed.
Sort these words. Cap and kit have short vowels. Cape and kite have long vowels made by silent e.
Look for the vowel, one consonant, and a final silent e.
Let us build one together. Start with tap. Add silent e. What word do you make? Tape.
The e stays silent. The a becomes long.
Your turn. Change hop into a word with a long o sound. Which letter will you add?
Add silent e: hope. The o says its name.
Remember the pattern: vowel, consonant, silent e. Cap becomes cape, kit becomes kite, and hop becomes hope.
Silent e is quiet, but powerful.
